reviews.text: Really enjoying the game so far. Seems to be a few ways to overcome the burdens of making money quickly. Like the permanent upgrades you can "earn" too. Fun in general.

It seems really well designed and implemented, unique even. On the surface, there appears to be a lot of different ways you can assemble your engine/tableau to get to the goal. It took me approx 2 hours to get my first successful run on the easiest difficulty, and I felt really satisfied in how I pieced it together after a few runs of tweaking the idea I had (I don't want to spoil how I did it but it did seem OP). I think others will enjoy digging into this and figuring out different engines to see how well designed and open the game really is, I am not good at analysing these things myself. On my next run to 3 million I'll try a different idea to see if I can make it effective. There's a lot of cool cards that I find interesting that I wasn't able to solve and I look forward to trying to build around them/breaking them. I feel like there's quite a bit of depth to explore and the game incentivises you to try it by taxing (with time) cards that won you the previous run, which is a cool idea (yet to see if it's frustrating) I also think I've done a good job at filtering out the trap cards. I still need to interact with buying more cards that could change how I put the puzzle together and I haven't explored past the starter upgrades - this is where the meta/prestige mechanics come in. Honestly I have not really payed much attention to this (yet) but going for higher numbers will no doubt need a bit of a grind to unlock tools to get you there (a good thing for incremental enthusiasts!) I'm imagining that I'll need to have runs where I simply maximise silver production for as long as I can before inevitably failing the money goal. But in short, I'm impressed with this. I didn't feel screwed over by RNG, only by my own bad choices which I think is good game design. The UI is clean and I think there's a huge amount of potential to develop the ideas presented here for future iterations - it does feel unique in the seamless marriage of different ideas. I would definitely recommend this game to people who are into active-incremental and engine building games (computer or board.) I would not say it's like other roguelike deckbuilders and has more in common with Zachtronic-type puzzle games than it does, say, Slay the Spire or Balatro. Assembling cool engines does scratch the same itch as putting together a nice engine in Opus Magnum or even putting the right cards down to do get your Magic The Gathering deck working smoothly. Good stuff, and the price makes it certainly worth a chance if what you see, or what I wrote, intrigues you. If the depth I'm seeing in the early stages is there then it honestly seems underpriced! Well done dev, I enjoyed your game for 2 hours already and no doubt will get a few more in.

Pretty fun, worth 7 bucks IMO. Edit: Still think this is worth 7 dollars, but the way it scales difficulty is pretty unfun. It isn't enough to find one good strategy that you can ride through the initial difficulty levels, you need to find a NEW strategy each time to get past the next level. The requirements scale up, but the cards you used to beat the previous level are debuffed. To me, this is a pretty poor design choice. As I work through a roguelite I want to refine a successful build up through the difficulties and slowly branch out. Getting pummeled till I learn a completely different strategy that's even stronger than my last win doesn't feel great. This just feels like a bit of a shallow way of forcing you to try different strategies rather than just making other strategies interesting. Its a fun game for a few hours, but it lacks the depth to make it repayable for hundreds of hours.

My numbers go up people!, there is something here, stay a spell and read. its worth it. edit: The foundation of this is rock solid. Im sure a lot of work has already gone into this. but if you duplicate a couple of work cards that you have stacked for 8 hours, and then duplicate that again, this could rise to the popularity of vampire survivor. in all seriousness, there is some mad scientist of numbers behind this and it leaves me wanting more of IT. please build more on top of this. or build a two. but do not stop making games.

Kinda sucks. To random. and tend to get more junk cards than any other card. Your first choice in the game determines if you will ever pass $2m... getting to $1m expect to restart atleast 10 times. The game itself tells you that it "will" become easier. I call BS. Then the lotto randomness at 1% ok fair. But the time for cycle being insanely high means that you have better odds with other cards. having a full board of Lotto cards won't help you to win. THEN you get to where "IF" you win a run - the cards you used to win the run with gets debuffed - fair enough 1 run ok , 2 runs ,ok , 5 runs, getting frustrated, all runs till you win again. Again calling BS. There is way to many variables and the matter of fact is you choice your own variables based on randomness THAT will inevitably cause you to do 100's of runs over without progressing. Then comes the "silver and gold coins". THESE add an additional randomness on to the INSANELY random features already impleminted. Choice to get a choice between 3 random cards. All being trash cards or save up 2 - 3 rounds worth of silver to get the SMALLEST of possible boosts to your run. PS. save your gold till you get 3 ( goodluck with that because it's easier said than done ) I have never raged on a game but damn man - it feels like this game was made by Satan himself. And no, I'm not trash at games and no I did not just do 2 runs and feel like commenting like I did. GL to the next person trying their b.ts off to win.

首先，这不是一个放置挂机游戏，是类小丑牌！如果冲着放置挂机来的可以先走了 为什么会得到上诉结论呢？以下是本人的游戏理解： 游戏首次是几乎不可能通关的，玩家的大多数东西都没解锁，需要简单的肝一下银币和金币，由于游戏内买牌越来越贵，普通的研究牌又有次数限制，纯靠出门那几张废物绝对打不过。不要迷信出门的1成长，那是小垃圾，有几张非常重要的牌需要解锁，解锁了开始变成爽游 献祭：销毁右侧卡牌并获得其收益。游戏内最无敌的终端，却又有极强的前期能力，出门吃2个50块的债券即可无压力度过前期 复制：生成右侧牌格相同的新卡牌。周期2。轮椅组件之一，可惜有次数限制2。 再融资：为随机研究牌增加1周期。轮椅组件之二，无脑辅助高收益研究牌（也就是上面的复制）直接开爽 好了，从这里开始就怎么爽都行了。能稳定度过前期后，有无限的复制就可以想玩什么玩什么，再也不用考虑去商店找指数级涨价的卡牌了。一直孵化器献祭也好，堆一个亿攻速玩扭亏为盈也行，铺一地研究牌养初始卡、甚至复制问号都可以乱杀，想怎么通关怎么通关。 那问题就在这里了，游戏内key牌解锁条件苛刻，而且没有就玩不了，这点很不利好肉鸽玩家。但对于放置挂机玩家呢？游戏给到的数值向局外成长对通关几乎没有任何帮助，两头不讨好了属于是。 如果能接受出门先坐俩小时牢然后开始狂按空格调牌序，那这游戏其实挺不错的。后续如果给玩家的初始卡组一些可复用的卡牌获取手段当教学我觉得就很不错了，现阶段在玩进去之前还是比较坐牢的，容易劝退轻度玩家啊 追加一下，如果游戏出个不限时通关的模式，我觉得就可以留下被增量游戏标签吸引来的玩家了。或者做成新手教程也不错，毕竟上来第一把一定会输的游戏是非常劝退玩家的。

Fun little engine building quota game. Very simple and intuitive structure and card ideas. Finding a way to completely break the game was fun, though this does make all the progression/challenges fairly boring once you have gone infinite. There is a daily challenge with a leaderboard and set cards so you cant go infinite which is a great addition to a game like this.

I kept unlocking things waiting for something interesting to happen, but it never does. Finally found the upgrades to see if they would improve more runs, but they really aren't so far. Earning them is incredibly grindy for very small benefit. I guess losing over and over for pocket change is kind of an incremental, but isn't fun.

Can't recommend it, unfortunately. I'd give a healthy 6/10. I could play this if a solar flare eradicates all other entertainment from existence but otherwise won't bother pushing past the 2 hours I've got. It's winnable but it feels super, super random. Unlocking cards feels more like a punishment mechanic to make the difficulty get worse over time than an upgrade. After the first few, the meta upgrades are microscopically worthless and slow. Fair to say however that if for some reason you like this it would probably take about a thousand hours to unlock everything. I wanted to like this one which is why I bought it but the deckbuilding aspect is poorly executed and the incremental aspect is more grueling than dopamine-loopy. I could forgive either of those if the other was good and we had a good deckbuilder (with some token upgrades) or we had a good incremental (where you pick cards) but we got neither. Recommended for fans of slot machines.

Fantastic so far, if you like incremental games and have a pretty good grasp of numbers. Some of the cards are in need of some balancing, but its very fun to play around with and test out builds. I had a bug pop up, but the developers were very responsive and got in touch via Discord and resolved it. Worth the buy, recommended.

I just can't recommend this game. Too many cards to unlock, complete randomization of cards earned in a run which is 99% of the reasons you lose a run, complete randomization of what cards you unlock, and not enough information on cards. The last point is really what pushed me to write this review. I just unlocked a card called copy. It says it will copy the card to the right every x number of seconds 1 time. I chose it from my random three gold coin card unlock thinking this could help snowball. I had a grow card on the field and put the copy next to it. my grow was already at 8. The copy triggered and a new grow card was added to my hand. It started out as a base 1 grow card, not a grow card of 8 value, so not an actual copy. If the card would have properly informed me of that, I would not have purchased it. Just overall more frustrating than fun. I don't know how many runs I bought my first card, saw all garbage, rerolled, more garbage, rerolled, same garbage and then just started a new run. Too much randomization and not enough information. Edit: I just reread copy. It says "Creates a new card in hand EQUAL to the card in the slot to the right..." so my expectations were correct, this card just didn't perform like it was written. Even worse.

A good game overall, has it's pros and cons. Pros: Many different interesting strategies to achieve the money goals. Some levels have different metas to keep user experience freshy. On later levels it becomes repetitive and slightly boring, but that's why daily challenge exists - a fantastic addition to keep players busy & entertained after completing a not-so-long journey. Cons: 1)Unlocking new cards is literally a punishment because it makes building certain strategies or farming silver much harder (by adding more cards to the pool to draw from). Once you bought all cards which contribute to your strategy, DO NOT buy any more of them unless you upgrade cards ban thingy to at least level 10+. 2)Too much randomness - every card draw is an RNG, every reroll is an RNG, luck chance, card generators, etc. Sometimes it feels like the luck is a more important factor for victory and not skill, which genuinely sucks especially in daily challenges which are meant to be competitive zone between players. They should display skill and not the amount of times people re-try a level to get a lucky attempt. 3)Forget the word 'Balance' exists, because here it clearly does not. Sometimes the chaos you could create is fun and all, but it just removes any point of challenge the game is supposed to offer, and it gives insane advantage over those who don't use the abuses like infinite games duration, infinite cards generator, and so on. Overall, I found this game fun and interesting to an extent. It has a fantastic potential to grow in further development, but also has many aspects to work with.

Not a super well balanced game. It's totally possible that the solution is "git gud", but I've played around with 7ish different builds and have gotten pretty much perfect conditions for several different solves to the exponential scaling of the difficulty. Only one of them worked, barely, and then the game nerfed the core card of that build because I won with it. The Bull and Bear mechanic is clearly meant to diversify build options, but the game cycles so quickly (~5 minutes per run when at max speed) that it ends up feeling like a drag. I've had one card in the Bear position for several days now... so I just haven't played it. If it cycled after every run it might be more fun. Part of the issue is that even for an incremental game, it feels like an incredible slog. A lot of the core mechanics are locked behind meta progression that you have to sacrifice runs in order to speed up progress towards. Incrementals generally feel good to me because I get a little further on every run. There's a sense of constant progress. This game feels like it *should* have that sense of progress, but it doesn't. After a dozen or so runs, your meta progress grinds to a halt, locked behind time itself (meta progress tokens are received every 20 seconds; you need 100 of them for the cheapest upgrades). At the end of the day, I don't feel like the game rewards you for trying to win, but rather for spending time in the game and completing a laundry list of tasks to make your runs unexcitingly better (e.g., +0.01 to your speed multiplier which starts at 1.20, amounting to a 0.83% increase in efficiency at best). Some of the cards are also pretty unsatisfying to stack up. Like there's a card that increases its value every time it's played. Classic linear rate progression. When you stack multiple of the cards, it increases the BASE value instead of the rate of increase. This punishes stacking the cards because you essentially halve the amount of value you get when you stack them. The mechanics feel like they're working against each other in that case, and this is not unique. To be absolutely clear, I like the concept. I think the tile placement is a fun puzzle and a lot of the cards are really interesting. The theming around speculative markets and day trader culture are really clever and cute. But when recognizing synergies and executing on them with good luck and clever card placement yields failures that feel pretty damn similar to when you get ♥♥♥♥ luck and pull random crap that barely synergizes... it's just not satisfying. I'll revisit and reconsider the review if there's a balance overhaul.

It's an interesting idea, but I agree with other folks that I found it really hard to get hooked. It's sort of fun in the beginning as you're messing around, but it quickly becomes a slog to just get a few cards that have synergy. Most runs die early due to not having cards that are very good. There is "progression" in the form of permanent unlocks, but the benefit they provide is extremely marginal compared to the amount of grinding required to actually unlock them. It's got some potential, the idea is definitely interesting, but the execution leaves a bit to be desired. I probably won't play it again unless there are some balance changes to mix things up.

Really trying to like this as "big numbers make brain go brrr", but like others say it feels like unlocking more cards actually makes things harder. The runs are dead in the water unless you get specific cards, and it feels too much like a slog to get anywhere half decent currently. I want to like it, I really do, but in its current state I just can't get hooked.

Though the balance of this initially felt off, it seems to have resolved itself. I do feel like I go for pretty similar setups every time, but at the very least most of the cards are interesting and suggest building around. Very enjoyable and chill game.

Its a good game for what it is, it however also breaks completely apart once you realize the interactions between the cards, so its more a case of going for the various challenges and "completing" everything.

It's a game where I think the demo was more compelling than how the full game played out. Here are some thoughts after getting the first difficulty completed: - The game offers you two meta currencies: silver and gold. Both can be used to buy new cards or flat upgrades. The page where you can buy new cards is presented first and, for silver, the per card cost is significantly lower than the per upgrade cost. I would have been much happier unlocking cards for achieving in a run vs. the current system. - Buying new cards before upgrades will make the game significantly harder to progress. In my opinion, either the upgrades should be front and center to encourage buying those first or (and probably better) these aren't on the same currency. The developer has since added a note in game to encourage buying upgrades first but it's still very easy to mess this up and have to crawl your way back. - Each meta upgrade takes an escalating amount of currency to purchase and each one feels very minimal (2% increase to this, 0.01x that). On the whole, they will matter but per upgrade they're both boring and minimal. The best way to overcome this is to build "silver farms," which are essentially throw-away runs for the express purpose of grinding currency. - Many of the unlocked cards feel counter productive initially. I'm sure that gets better later with upgrades and synergies but until you get to that point the game just gets harder every time you unlock another card. Overall, I had a good time with this game and I was excited to see more after the demo but was disappointed at what was there.
grind to win meta progression

Nice little incremental card optimization game with a decent free demo to show you how it plays. Unlike a lot of other reviews, I found that it wasn't really grindy at all: There are several builds that can consistently win runs (and this is without simply getting infinite time to make money through a set of good synergies). A nice little "win penalty" on one of the Asset cards you used to win your last run with is a nice little encouragement to mix up your strategies at least a little between games, and it's fun trying to beat all the little challenges to unlock stuff. It does need to be said though: You need to be careful about unlocking cards before you build a good banlist, or each unlocked card might make the game [b]harder[/b] by making it harder to get the synergies you want. The dev's definitely made it harder to fall into this newb trap by giving you 5 free bans when you start and making card costs scale, but beware because you can still kinda "brick" your save if you don't focus on upgrades, too.

[b]TldR[/b] I never recommend stuff to people I don't know. But I like trying to understand finance stuff, I like NGU and [b]I like this game[/b]. So if you also like staring at a stock chart without fully getting it, and if ngu also give dopamine for your brain, then you like might also like this game. [b]Why did I buy the game?[/b] A couple of weeks ago I was in a lowkey sad mood and hoping for a way to escape reality for a bit, I got hit with a nostalgic brainwave and decided to go to Armorgames to play some old flash game classics. There I ran into the demo for this game. I played it, liked it and decided to buy the game if the prices wasn't too high as a thank you to the makers, even if I wasn't going to play it anymore. If only for the amount of time I spend playing the demo. I am happy I did, I like the full versions as well. [b]would I recommend this game?[/b] Everytime I open the game, steam keeps confronting me with amount of hours I played so far, only to keep asking me if I would recommend this game to other. Personally I don't recommending stuff to people, especially people I don't know, because experiences are very personal. I don't know you, I don't know what you like and things you don't like. So for as far as to recommending or not, the best thing I can come up with is making 2 lists of things the might increase or decrease the likely hood you will like this. start: 50% (you either like it or you don't, 50/50) +5% if you like finance +5% if you like ngu +10% if you like optimization puzzles +5% if you like a daily challenge with a specific subset of the game +5% if you have more than one of the boxes above ticked. (I think the game combines elements well imo.) -10% if you can easily get overwhelmed and don't like to slow down to focus on the basics -20% if you don't like finance -20% if you don't like numbers [b]what I think the average person can expect[/b] I think this is a game that can divide crowd. I know people that will absolutely hate this game, if only for the fact that the theme of finance can make it harder for some people to get into it, because not everybody likes thinking about finance. On the other hand I also now people that would instantly play this for 3 hours straight. If you're looking for a game to pass some time and you don't instantly hate it, Then I think you'll probably get a Euro/hours_played-value of less then 50 cents per hour. Which I think is good.
Number goes up. The simplicity helps it be an addicting iterative experience

Summary: Summary: I recommend this game, but don't expect too much from it. A solid indie effort. The First Million is an incremental card-based game where you buy cards and place them on a grid. The goal is to make a sufficient amount of money in the allotted time to move on to the next time gate. There are cards that make money directly, cards that scale other cards or provide other bonuses, and cards that increase global stats or improve other cards but burn out. The game is fun, but relatively easy to solve. This isn't Slay the Spire. There are only a few ways to win, and most cards don't do a ton to advance you to that. Especially on higher difficulties. You'll need to unlock the cards you need (like Subsidiary) and avoid the cards that don't help. The game allows you to block a certain number of cards from appearing at the beginning of a run, and you'll want to use that feature. It's a bit of a feels-bad nonetheless, because one of the achievements requires you to unlock all cards, and you need to complete achievements to both earn meta progression and unlock higher difficulty levels. I completed all achievements in about 9 hours. To be fair, I also played the demo for maybe 6. I lost my first few runs, because you need to unlock cards. I lost a couple of runs trying for the achievement where you don't use purple cards, and I lost my first attempt on the hardest difficulty because I was trying to avoid the most powerful strategy. And I lost a run intentionally as part of completing the achievement where you use the Insurance card three times. Otherwise, I won them all and it was rarely close. This is because the game is all about scaling. Certain cards do that, and most don't. The card pool isn't so large that you can't find the good ones, especially since you can unlock the ability to start with a universal tutor at the start and then buy it again repeatedly later. The developer tries to balance this. If you win a run, the card that made the most money for you will be debuffed for your next runs until you win. There's also a buffed card and a debuffed card that changes daily. The issue is, it doesn't really matter. I lost my first try at a max difficulty run because I tried to avoid the most powerful card (Sacrifice) as it was debuffed. Then I realized that it doesn't matter, and I used my usual strategy the next run and won handily, despite the debuff. This is understandable. In the end, the game is a math problem. The only real source of randomness is which card you're offered. There are a few other random elements but you can either play around them (blue cards that buff a random card of a type) or have so many opportunities to proc that the Law of Large Numbers kicks in and in the end, the behavior isn't meaningfully random (Lucky Chance). There are daily runs that challenge you to make as much money as possible with a small and random card pool. If you want a bunch of replay value, this is how you'll get it. I think it will be a little too easy to identify what to aim for each time though, because again, the game is all about scaling. So if you're the sort of person who really likes taking Demon Form in Slay the Spire, this is the game for you. The game appears to be in active development, so be aware that this review might be very out-of-date later.
im more interested in the daily + leaderboard than the base game

Very fun core loop, its a nice little incremental game. There are some strategies that are just S tier, but the Challenges provide enough variation to push you to try other stuff. The dev seems to be actively balancing which is nice to see. The additional opportunities to remove cards from the pool is great, lets you try things out without restarting over and over again.
Great little game that I kept coming back to.

Not a bad game, but also not a fun one. Could be alright if you enjoy dry math sandboxes (like me). Things to consider: — When playing, you don't care about game theme at all. After 30+ hours in the game I remember only Lottery, Insurance and Startup. All other cards are perceived by their effects, not the name. — You need to create your own goals. While game has variety of challenges and requires you to complete them, you can complete most of them with the same one combo you've found. So forcing yourself to try new things is necessary to create some variety of runs. — Constant pause-unpause is annoying, yet necessary for min-maxing. — UI is horrible. Card tooltips are constantly on the screen, blocking the view of the board. Elements resize, appear and disappear constantly, creating a visual chaos. Dragging a card is a puzzle by itself. Still, very good job for your first game!

I enjoyed the game until I won. Then the game nerfed the strategy I was using by 20% until I play a different strategy. While the idea of needing to have two different strategies is not the end of the world. The fact that the game forces it kinda ruined the fun. You find a build and perfect it after multiple runs then it wins you a run after all that work. Instead of being able to test it again, you are immediately punished by the game for winning until you do it again but different.
Very cool concept, hard to go away from "one more run". I would say its pretty hard for me, but im keep trying
An interesting mix of incremental and deckbuilder; it stretches the definition of post-balatro but it does have the increasing requirements element. Worth a look.
